questions.question_text: How would you design a globally distributed real-time notification engine for Netflix that can deliver 100M push messages per hour with at-least-once delivery semantics?
questions.ideal_answer: Design utilizing partitioned Apache Kafka topics or AWS SQS with distributed consumer workers, Redis cluster for deduplication caching (idempotency key TTL), Cassandra/DynamoDB for append-only delivery receipts, and backpressure mechanisms with dead-letter queues (DLQ) for failed device tokens.

questions.question_text: Walk me through your database sharding and partitioning strategy when scaling user activity feeds beyond a single relational database instance.
questions.ideal_answer: Use consistent hashing on user_id with virtual nodes to avoid rebalancing hotspots. Implement read replicas for feed queries, separate hot feeds into Redis sorted sets, and use fan-out-on-write for standard users with fan-out-on-read for high-follower celebrity accounts.

questions.question_text: How do you address cache stampedes, hot partition keys, and cache-aside invalidation in a multi-region Redis deployment at Netflix?
questions.ideal_answer: Prevent stampedes with Probabilistic Early Expiration (XFetch algorithm) or distributed mutex locks. Distribute hot keys via random salt suffixes. Invalidate via event-driven CDC (Change Data Capture) over Kafka, and leverage Redis Active-Active multi-region replication.

questions.question_text: In building high-performance modern web platforms for Google, how do you manage state synchronization, WebSocket reconnect backoffs, and optimistic UI updates?
questions.ideal_answer:
1. State Sync: Event-driven client cache (TanStack Query / normalized store) with monotonic version IDs for conflict resolution.
2. WebSockets: Exponential backoff with full randomized jitter (e.g., 500ms doubling to 10s ceiling with ±20% jitter) to eliminate thundering herd connection spikes. Pair with heartbeat pings/pongs.
3. Optimistic UI: Apply mutation immediately to local cache with temporary ID and snapshot rollback buffer; reconcile upon canonical server ack.

questions.question_text: Given an array of incoming HTTP requests with timestamps and IP addresses, write an algorithm to determine if an IP has exceeded a rate limit of 10 requests per 10-second window.
questions.ideal_answer: Sliding Window Log algorithm: For each IP, maintain a deque of timestamps. On request arrival at T, prune timestamps older than (T - 10,000ms). If queue length >= 10, reject with HTTP 429 and Retry-After header; otherwise append T and allow. In distributed production, execute atomically in Redis using a Sorted Set (ZREMRANGEBYSCORE + ZADD + ZCARD) wrapped in an EVAL Lua script to eliminate race conditions.

questions.question_text: Explain how the Node.js event loop coordinates timers, I/O polling, and microtasks, and how unhandled Promise rejections affect application stability in production.
questions.ideal_answer: Event loop runs phases: Timers -> Pending callbacks -> Poll (I/O) -> Check (setImmediate) -> Close callbacks. Microtasks (process.nextTick, Promise .then) run immediately between phase transitions with priority. Unhandled Promise rejections trigger unhandledRejection events and terminate the Node process in modern versions, potentially leaking connection pool resources and crashing pods.
